senses.gloss:
śauca
(‘cleanliness,’ ‘purity’)
------------------------------------------
The Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) lists शौच or purity as one of the five disciplines under नियम, the second of the eight steps of योग.
It is of two kinds: bāhya or external; āntara or internal. The former is achieved by cleansing the body and the latter, by conquering the six-enemies like lust and greed.
It is interesting to note that the Manusmṛti (5.106) considers purity in financial dealings as the real or the best purity.
The धर्मशास्त्रस् and the various smṛtis give a detailed account of आह्निक or the daily routine of a द्विज (a member of the first three castes). शौच or bodily purity is an important part of the same.
